text.p: Greg Norman was in the thick of the battle as the birdie chase began on the opening holes of the British Open at Royal Troon on Thursday.
With a stiff breeze at his back, the champion in 1986 and 1993 parred the first two holes before collecting birdies at the third and fourth to share the lead with four others.
He rammed in a 10-foot putt on the 379-yard third and hit his second through the green at the 557-yard par-five fourth before chipping back to three feet and holing for birdie.

But even with the favourable wind, conditions were not easy and the paramount problem for the players was how to play approach shots. They had the choice of flying them on to the green and hoping they stopped or landing them short and letting them roll on.

Local hero Colin Montgomerie, world number four and another of the favourites, bounded through the first green but salvaged par after a good chip and finished at the back of the second and third greens, two-putting for par each time.
Promising newcomer Lee Westwood of Britain was among those level with Norman after birdies at the 364-yard first, where he drove the green, and the fourth.
Aslo on two-under were Retief Goosen of South Africa, Argentine Eduardo Romero, Australian Peter Lonard and American Scott McCarron.
Hot favourite Tiger Woods was due off at 1205 GMT.
